sections.heading: Each {{entity_noun}} you identify qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: The record's mentions evidence the {{entity_noun}} you identified — it is named, described, or clearly implied by what the mentions say, not merely suggested by a resemblance between words.

children.text: Whose {{entity_noun}} it is has no bearing here. A candidate evidenced by a customer's, supplier's, or any other third party's dealings is still identified and recorded.

The {{entity_noun}} must be identifiable as an operation performed on the work. A business, legal, or contractual undertaking that describes how a company deals with other parties rather than what is done to the work identifies no {{entity_noun}}; neither does a certification, credential, program, or philosophy about quality or improvement that names no operation performed on the work, nor general praise of experience, service, or capability that names no particular operation. Inspection, testing, and measurement performed on the work are operations, and are identifiable as a {{entity_noun}}.

rules.text: The {{entity_noun}} you identified is of the kind {{entity_noun}} names, judged against what {{entity_noun}} means. A business or contractual undertaking, a certification or credential, a program or philosophy, general praise of capability, or anything else outside that meaning does not qualify, however clearly the record evidences it.

Neither the provided options nor the record's already-identified results cover the {{entity_noun}} you identified: no option matches it exactly or under different words, judged against {{option_evidence}}, and it does not restate an already-identified result.
